articles.title: Una carrera capital: llega el Derbi de las Aficiones entre 'indios' y 'vikingos'
articles.standfirst: Casi 11.000 corredores disputarán este domingo el Derbi de las Aficiones Aliexpress Marcas+ Chuwi, unos 10k homologados, en busca de marcas y de la victoria de su ‘equipo’
articles.summary: Casi 11.000 corredores disputarán este domingo el Derbi de las Aficiones Aliexpress Marcas+ Chuwi, unos 10k homologados, en busca de marcas y de la victoria de su ‘equipo’
articles.body: Unos persiguen la remontada, otros buscan la ‘Décima’. ‘Indios’ y ‘vikingos’ se retan este domingo de nuevo sobre el asfalto (9.00 horas) en la decimosexta edición del Derbi de las Aficiones Aliexpress Marcas+ Chuwi. Desde la salida, en los aledaños del Santiago Bernabéu, hasta la meta, junto al antiguo Vicente Calderón, los aficionados de ambos equipos volverán a demostrar que la deportividad no está reñida con la pasión por los colores de tu equipo. Pese a que se trata de una prueba individual, el esfuerzo de todos los corredores, sea cual sea su nivel de forma, tiene premio, ya que los tiempos de todos los participantes contarán para el resultado final de este duelo capital que dominan los ‘vikingos’ en el tanteo histórico de la carrera, por 9-6. El perfil descendente de estos 10 kilómetros está homologado por la Real Federación Española de atletismo, por lo que se convierte en una gran oportunidad para hacer un buen registro con vistas a otras carreras, como la Nationale-Nederlanden San Silvestre Vallecana. Sin duda, el recorrido será un aliado para los corredores, que transitarán por muchos puntos emblemáticos para las aficiones de ambos equipos, como el Bernabéu, Cibeles, Neptuno, el antiguo Calderón... En esta edición, competirán el doble ganador del Derbi de las Aficiones Aliexpress Marcas+ Chuwi, Nicolás Regidor, así como atletas de referencia de la Comunidad de Madrid, como Rodrigo Mendoza o Sergio Fernández. Aunque la victoria final será para una de las aficiones, hay que recordar que Alejandro Jiménez (28:37) y Lucía Rodríguez (31:34) ostentan los récords individuales de la prueba por el momento. Las calles de Madrid se teñirán mañana de blanco y rojo, con ‘indios’ y ‘vikingos’ dirimiendo a zancadas qué equipo domina en el derbi de la capital. Será la decimosexta edición de una fiesta con un marcado tinte futbolero y buen rollo que tiene a Aliexpress Marcas+ Chuwi como patrocinador principal, además de contar con el impulso de Cabify, BM Supermercados y Hersamotor, junto a la colaboración del Ayuntamiento de Madrid. ¿Habrá ‘Décima’ o será el inicio de la remontada?

articles.title: Simone Biles, The Champion Who Refused to Let the World Define Her
articles.summary: From overcoming a difficult childhood to becoming one of the greatest gymnasts in history, Simone Biles has proved her strength goes far beyond the gym
articles.body:
Simone Biles has transformed what athletic greatness looks like in gymnastics. Standing 4 feet 8 inches tall, she has combined extraordinary power, precision and technical difficulty to build one of the most decorated careers the sport has ever seen. Her achievements stretch across multiple Olympic Games and World Championships, but medals tell only part of her story. Biles has also changed conversations around pressure, mental health and the expectations placed on elite athletes. Her journey has become as much about resilience as dominance.

Born in Ohio in 1997, Biles experienced instability during her early childhood as she and her siblings spent time in foster care. Her maternal grandfather, Ron Biles, and his wife, Nellie, eventually adopted Simone and her younger sister Adria. Biles discovered gymnastics at age six during a daycare field trip, and her natural ability quickly became apparent. By her teenage years, she was competing at the elite level and beginning a rise that would reshape women's gymnastics.

Her international breakthrough came before the 2016 Rio Olympics, where she arrived as the sport's biggest star. Biles won four gold medals in Rio, taking titles in the team competition, individual all around, vault and floor exercise, as well as a bronze on balance beam. Her explosive tumbling and exceptional difficulty helped establish a new standard for what was possible in women's gymnastics.

The next chapter proved far more complicated. At the Tokyo Olympics, held in 2021 after a pandemic delay, Biles withdrew from several events after experiencing the twisties, a dangerous loss of spatial awareness while performing aerial skills. With gymnasts rotating and flipping at high speed, losing that awareness can create a serious risk of injury. Her decision placed athlete wellbeing at the center of an international conversation about competition and mental health.

Biles eventually returned for the balance beam final and earned a bronze medal, but she stepped away from competitive gymnastics afterward. Rather than ending her career, the break became another turning point. She returned to competition in 2023 and quickly demonstrated that she could once again perform at the highest level.

At the Paris Olympics in 2024, Biles completed one of sport's most remarkable comebacks. She captured gold medals in the team event, individual all around and vault, along with silver on floor exercise. Those results brought her career Olympic total to 11 medals, making her the most decorated U.S. Olympic gymnast.

Her influence reaches beyond the medal table. Biles has openly discussed therapy, anxiety and the importance of protecting mental wellbeing, challenging the idea that elite athletes must ignore personal struggles to prove their toughness.

Biles has spent her career expanding the limits of gymnastics, but perhaps her greatest legacy is broader. She has shown that strength can mean attempting skills few others can perform, stepping away when safety demands it, and finding the courage to return on your own terms.

articles.title: Northern Olympics plan to get £7m in John Healey's first Budget
articles.summary: The full feasibility study will look in detail at how hosting the Games in northern England could work.
articles.body:
A £7m fund to explore how the Olympics could be brought to northern England will be announced in John Healey's first Budget on Wednesday, the BBC has learned.

The chancellor plans to allocate the money for a full feasibility study on the possibility for a bid for a "Northern Games".

If successful, it could see the games held in the North in the 2040s.

The last time the UK hosted the Olympics was London 2012. A UK Trade and Investment (UKTI) department report estimated in 2013 it boosted the economy by £9.9bn, although the amount was met with some scepticism.

Olympians join mayors to back northern Olympic bid

Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the BBC: "Few things bring a country together quite like the Olympics. I want people to feel that sense of excitement again, and to experience it in their own towns and communities, not just watch it on the telly.

"The Games would unlock opportunity across our towns and cities for the whole country. From north to south, it would be something everyone could get behind and be proud of.

"We know we can put on the greatest show on earth. Now we want to explore how we can do it again, with the whole country behind it."

In May the government asked UK Sport to carry out an initial assessment of the idea, looking at the possible cost and benefit of a bid to hold the Olympics across the North.

The idea had been put forward by Northern Mayors and backed by a group of former Olympians including Dame Laura Kenny and Dame Sarah Storey.

As part of next week's Budget the government will announce the next step - a "full feasibility study".

The report will look in closer detail at how hosting the games could work.

It will consider the kinds of venues and transport links required, how different cities could share the games, how communities could benefit.

Crucially it will also examine how much it could cost as well as assess the chances of a bid succeeding. The Conservative-Lib Dem coalition government said in 2013 it estimated hosting in London had cost £8.9bn.

A report in 2013 by the UK Trade and Investment, which has since been replaced by the Department for International Trade, said it had sparked a £9.9bn boost to the economy through new contracts, sales and foreign investments.

But the estimated amount was queried by some, including the Federation of Small Businesses and the National Institute of Economic and Social Research (NIESR) .

The new feasability study for the Northern Games will be done by government, UK Sport, the Northern Mayors and include the British Olympic and Paralympic associations.

Healey said: "Olympic legacy lasts way beyond the celebration of sport over the summer. The North hosting an event as big as this would be truly unforgettable.

"Britain's experience of London 2012 is proof we can host the world. I'm picking up the pace on our work to potentially bid for these prestigious games. It will lift communities, create opportunities and give the UK a huge boost."

News of the funding for the study was welcomed by the British Olympic Association, ParalympicsGB and UK Sport.

"We welcome the government's continued support for exploring the potential of a future bid for the Olympic and Paralympic Games in the UK in the 2040s," they said in a joint statement.

"Building on the success and legacy of London 2012, we look forward to working in partnership to explore this exciting opportunity and the benefits it could deliver for the nation, and for the global Olympic and Paralympic movements."

articles.title: A Bulgarian Sports Official and Former Member of European Parliament Shot Dead
articles.summary: SOFIA, Bulgaria (AP) — The head of the Bulgarian Taekwondo Federation and vice president of the European Taekwondo Union was shot dead on Saturday at his home in Sofia, police said.
articles.body:
SOFIA, Bulgaria (AP) — The head of the Bulgarian Taekwondo Federation and vice president of the European Taekwondo Union was shot dead on Saturday at his home in Sofia, police said.

Slavi Binev, 60, had switched to politics after a successful career as Taekwondo fighter to become member of the National Assembly and of the European Parliament elected on the ticket of nationalist parties.

Police received a call about gunfire around 10:30 a.m. and found him dead when they arrived at the scene. An investigation is underway.

Top police officer Lyubomir Nikolov told reporters that three suspects were detained on a highway outside Sofia.

Nikolov said two of the suspects had Turkish citizenship, while the third held a Bulgarian ID card. He added that they were armed but did not elaborate about possible motives of the crime.

Local media reported about his activities in the early 1990s, linked to a group that ran several entertainment venues in Sofia and was allegedly involved in prostitution, drugs and trafficking of stolen cars.

During the 1990s, mafia-style killings of public figures were a common occurrence in Bulgaria. The death of Binev is the latest of a new sequence of high-profile killings. It coincided with the end of a heated campaign for Sunday's presidential elections.

articles.title: Election of IOA Athletes’ Commission: 9 sports, 10 seats and uneven representation
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: With 12 athletes from nine sports in the fray for 10 elected positions in the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) Athletes’ Commission, the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With 12 athletes from nine sports in the fray for 10 elected positions in the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) Athletes’ Commission, the application of a key provision in the election rules has emerged as an important consideration -- how to ensure maximum representation of different sports in the Commission.Rule 8.6 of the IOA Athletes’ Commission Rules, 2026 states that, “as far as practicable”, the composition of the Commission should seek “maximum representation from all sports affiliated with IOA”. It adds that, as a guiding principle, “an endeavour shall be made to ensure that there is not more than one Athlete from any one particular sport”.The provision assumes significance in the ongoing election, with the draft list of nominations showing candidates from nine sports competing for 10 positions — five male and five female.The 12 nominees are Manjeet Singh (kayaking and canoeing), Swapnil Suresh Kusale (shooting), Harmanpreet Singh (hockey), Sajan Prakash (swimming), Kidambi Srikanth (badminton) and Tajinderpal Singh Toor (athletics) in the male category.The female nominees are PV Sindhu (badminton), Salima Tete (hockey), Mirabai Chanu (weightlifting), L Bombayla Devi (archery), Sudha Singh (athletics) and Bhavani Devi (fencing).Athletics, badminton and hockey have candidates in both the male and female categories. The remaining six sports have one nominee each.An opportunity to maximise diversityThe current nomination pattern presents an opportunity to give representation to all nine sports in the 10-member Commission, with one sport having two representatives.Such a composition would align with the guiding principle under Rule 8.6, provided the mandatory eligibility and category requirements are met and the outcome is consistent with the prescribed election process.The provision does not, however, establish a separate quota for each sport or specify which sport should have two representatives. Nor does it expressly authorise the Electoral Officer (Returning Officer) to override the election outcome to achieve a preferred composition.Instead, the wording places emphasis on what is practicable and calls for an endeavour to avoid multiple representatives from the same sport.Mandatory requirements remain centralThe Rules also prescribe specific requirements for the Commission’s composition. Under Rule 8.1, the 10 elected members must comprise five male and five female athletes.Rule 8.2 provides that six of the elected members must have participated in at least one of the last three editions of the Olympic Games. Rule 8.3 specifies that these six must include three male and three female athletes.The remaining four members, under Rule 8.5, must feature two male and two female athletes who have won at least one medal in any of the last three editions of the Asian Games, Commonwealth Games, World Championship/Cup or National Games.Rule 8.4 further states that, as far as practicable, the Olympic-category composition should include at least one athlete from an individual sport and at least one from a team sport.The final composition must give effect to these requirements alongside the guiding principle of maximum sporting representation.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Paula Moltzan golpea primero con el gran triunfo de su vida
articles.standfirst: A sus 32 años, conquista el Gigante de Sölden para lograr la primera victoria de su carrera en la Copa del Mundo, mientras Mikaela Shiffrin pasó de dominar la manga inicial a ser séptima
articles.summary: A sus 32 años, conquista el Gigante de Sölden para lograr la primera victoria de su carrera en la Copa del Mundo, mientras Mikaela Shiffrin pasó de dominar la manga inicial a ser séptima
articles.body: La Copa del Mundo ya está aquí. La 61ª edición se ha puesto en marcha donde lo hace cada año desde 2001. El glaciar de Rettenbach vuelve a ser el punto de partida. En Sölden se da el banderazo de salida a una temporada que arranca con el gigante femenino. Una campaña ya sin una de las más grandes de todos los tiempos, Lara Gut. La retirada de la suiza y las ausencias de las italianas Brignone y Goggia estaban en un lado de la balanza; en el otro, la batalla por la primera victoria de la temporada. La apertura de la competición en la exigente Rettenbach, marcada por el equipo noruego, fue para la neozelandesa Alice Robinson, que detuvo el crono en 1:08.63. La segunda en bajar fue la mejor gigantista de la temporada pasada y ganadora hace un año en Sölden: la austriaca Julia Scheib. Y para ella fue la primera caída de la temporada. Una mala lectura con el pie izquierdo le hizo perder el equilibrio y caer de mala manera. Se mantiene la tradición que dice que ninguna mujer ha sido capaz de ganar dos años seguidos en Sölden. Con Scheib fuera de combate, la sueca Sara Hector lanzó la batalla real por la victoria. La de Sandviken pulverizó el tiempo de Robinson (-1.22). Y su registro lo rebajó la de siempre: Mikaela Shiffrin. La temporada en la que la gran reina del esquí mundial quiere centrar esfuerzos en el Gigante y el Súper arrancaba con Shiffrin como la mejor en la primera manga. Lo mismo que había logrado en 31 ocasiones en los 110 Gigantes previos. El anterior, el 30 de noviembre de 2024, cuando luego se cayó en Killington para sufrir la lesión costal que tantos problemas le causó. Al terreno marcado por Shiffrin se acercaron cinco corredoras por debajo del segundo de diferencia: Sara Hector (+0.14), Camille Rast (+0.37), Britt Richardson (+0.53), Paula Moltzan (+0.59) y Lara Colturi (+0.78). Entre ellas debía estar el triunfo. El estreno de la temporada traía el regreso a la Copa del Mundo de dos grandes. La eslovaca Petra Vlhova no aparecía desde enero de 2024, cuando se cayó en Jasna y sufrió una grave lesión de rodilla que le causó un sinnúmero de problemas. Petra bajó con solvencia para lograr un crono a 1.31 de Shiffrin que la colocaba entre las diez primeras. Un gran regreso. El otro era el de una ganadora en Sölden (2020) y una de las mejores gigantistas de la década. Marta Bassino volvía después de perderse toda la temporada pasada por una caída sufrida a cuatro días del arranque en Sölden. Corta de preparación y en busca de sensaciones, la italiana bajó con la mente puesta en llegar antes que en firmar un buen tiempo. Llegó a más de tres segundos, pero con una sonrisa en la cara aunque se quedar fuera del corte de las 30 mejores. Ese corte, el de las 30 mejores para la segunda manga, lo marcó la suiza Vanessa Kasper, que se fue a 2.54 de Mikaela Shiffrin. Marcado el trazado decisivo por el equipo italiano, la bajada final se presentaba con un esquema conocido: todas contra el Expreso de Vail. Y Mikaela en busca de la victoria en un gigante, algo no visto desde el 28 de diciembre de 2023, el de Lienz. Con los ojos puestos en las cinco últimas bajadas, las de las esquiadoras que estaban a menos de un segundo, las corredoras iban llegando a meta. Con una visibilidad que menguaba, el objetivo de las que se sabían fuera de la pelea por la victoria era arrancar la temporada con buenas sensaciones. Como lo hizo la polaca Maryna Gasienica-Daniel, que comandó la prueba gracias a tres sectores imponentes hasta la bajada de la decimoquinta mejor clasificada de la primera manga: Asja Zenere. La italiana pasó de estar a punto de caerse a dominar la prueba. Con solo una austriaca entre las 30 mejores, Franziska Gritsch, el triunfo local estaba descartado tras la caída de Scheib. El mando de Zenere la catapultó entre las diez primeras y no dejó el sillón de líder hasta la bajada de Emma Aicher. La alemana, la mujer que corre las cuatro especialidades, mejoró el crono en veinte centésimas para sumar puntos en la disciplina que más le cuesta y en la que su mejor resultado era una cuarta plaza. Entonces apareció en escena Lara Colturi. La italiana que corre para Albania firmó una bajada excelsa, con problemas en el muro central, pero imponente en el resto. Se colocó primera cuando sólo quedaban cinco por bajar. Pero le duró poco el liderato, porque se lo arrebató la siguiente en bajar: Paula Moltzan, por una centésima. La gran batalla estaba desatada. Falló la canadiense Richardson (+2.29) y solo quedaban ya las mejores de la primera manga. A la suiza Rast se le puso la pista cuesta arriba desde el inicio. Acumuló tiempo en contra para quedarse sin opciones de podio. Moltzan tenía asegurado el podio y era la hora de Sara Hector. Para la sueca fue casi lo mismo que para Rast. Se le fue todo y también quedó fuera de las tres primeras Y faltaba Shiffrin, sabiendo ya que la victoria era para Estados Unidos. Mikaela vivió los mismos problemas que Rast y Hector. Incluso más. La luz cambiante, el viento y la nieve complicaron la bajada de las tres mejores de la primera manga. Shiffrin se fue hasta la séptima plaza. Y la sonrisa de Moltzan se disparó. Era su primera victoria en la Copa del Mundo. "Es increíble, tengo que tomarme tiempo para asimilarlo", explicaba la de Minnesota a Eurosport tras su victoria. Tiene 32 años. A su lado, Lara Colturi y Emma Aicher. Ese fue el orden final en Sölden. Dentro de dos semanas, las mujeres volverán a la nieve en el eslalon de Levi. La victoria de Shiffrin en gigante deberá esperar.

articles.title: P V Sindhu defeats Japan's Akechi 21-10, 20-22, 21-16; sets up French Open title clash with world No. 1 An Se Young
articles.summary: Two-time Olympic medallist P V Sindhu reached her second Super 750 final of the year after beating Japan's Hina Akechi in a three-game battle at the
articles.body: Two-time Olympic medallist P V Sindhu reached her second Super 750 final of the year after beating Japan's Hina Akechi in a three-game battle at the French Open in Paris on Saturday.The 31-year-old Indian, who won the Japan Open Super 750 title in July, defeated world No. 22 Akechi 21-10, 20-22, 21-16 in an hour and 13 minutes."I am a little bit happy that I could pull off the match and play the finals, but I think the job is not done yet and I think I need to go back and focus for one more match," Sindhu said.Akechi, 21, had beaten Wang Zhi Yi and Putri Kusuma Wardani earlier in the week. She used her deceptive strokes and defence to put Sindhu under pressure, but the Indian held on to win the deciding game and book her place in the final.Sindhu will face world No. 1 An Se Young of South Korea in Sunday's title clash."I have to give her a good fight, a tough fight. Every point matters. We've played a lot of times and she's been doing really well," she said."She's been at her top form, but I think tomorrow is a different day. I just have to just go out there and give my best."The opening game was closely fought in the early stages, with the scores level at 4-4 and 8-8. Sindhu then moved ahead and took an 11-9 lead into the interval.The Indian stepped up after the break, winning 11 of the next 12 points to close out the game 21-10 in 18 minutes.Sindhu fell four points behind early in the second game but fought back to level the score at 7-7. Her round-the-head cross-court attacks produced winners as the two players remained level at 10-10 before Akechi began to edge ahead.The world No. 11 Indian kept pace with her opponent and drew level at 14-14. A cross-court smash helped her make it 16-16 before a deceptive return put her ahead.Akechi responded to earn a game point, which Sindhu saved at 20-20 after a rally at the net. The Japanese secured another game point and converted it when Sindhu hit wide, forcing a decider.Sindhu made a 5-3 start in the third game, but Akechi fought back to take a 6-5 lead. The Indian regained the advantage and went into the interval two points ahead, though she struggled to maintain consistency with her attacking shots.A cross-court return and a net shot helped Sindhu extend her lead, but Akechi fought back with accurate net play and a smash to level the score at 15-15.The turning point came during a 38-shot rally that ended with Akechi making an error at the net, allowing Sindhu to move ahead 18-16. Another well-placed net shot took the Indian closer to victory before Akechi hit wide to give her four match points.Sindhu sealed the win with a cross-court smash.The Indian has enjoyed a productive year, winning the Japan Open title in July and coming close to winning medals at the World Championships in New Delhi and the Asian Games. She will now have another opportunity to add a Super 750 title when she faces An Se Young in the final.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: El veterano Xu Jiayu bate el récord del mundo de 50 espalda
articles.standfirst: El chino de 31 años arrebata al sudafricano Coetze una plusmarca que le ha durado 15 días
articles.summary: El chino de 31 años arrebata al sudafricano Coetze una plusmarca que le ha durado 15 días
articles.body: Hay récords que duran una eternidad -el de 200 libre en piscina larga pasa de 17 años- y otros un suspiro. Apenas 15 días después de que el sudafricano Pierre Coetze en la Copa del Mundo de Tashkent (Uzbekistán) batiera la plusmarca de 50 espalda e piscina de 25 metros, el chino Xu Jiayu le arrebató la primacía. A los 31 años, una edad ya adulta para los nadadores, el plata en 100 metros espalda en Río mordió seis centésimas los 22.09 que había acreditado Coetze para dejar el récord en 22.03. en la primera posta de los Campeonatos Nacionales Chinos de los 4x50 estilos. El Cubo de Pekín, el escenario que asistió en 2008 a la mayor gesta de la historia de la natación en los Juegos Olímpicos con las ocho medallas de oro de Michael Phelps, asistió a un día redondo de Jiayu, que previamente había batido el récord asiático de 100 espalda con 48.77, la séptima mejor marca de todos los tiempos. Su figura, un especialista rotundo que ganó el oro con el relevo corto de estilos en París 2024, parece resurgir en estos Campeonatos donde ha ganado tres pruebas.

articles.title: Rebeca Andrade, Simone Biles’ Paris rival, is back and winning gymnastics gold again
articles.summary: ROTTERDAM, Netherlands — Simone Biles has spent much of her career leaving the rest of gymnastics behind, but Rebeca Andrade did something almost nobody else...
articles.body:
ROTTERDAM, Netherlands — Simone Biles has spent much of her career leaving the rest of gymnastics behind, but Rebeca Andrade did something almost nobody else could — she made the greatest gymnast in history look over her shoulder.

On Saturday, Andrade won her third world vault title in Rotterdam, joining China's Cheng Fei as the only women to achieve the feat and taking her career tally to 10 World Championships medals.

The Brazilian, 27, returned to the World Championships after three years away, five knee operations and a decision to abandon the floor exercise, in which she defeated Biles at the Paris Olympics, in hopes that a reduced programme could keep her at the top of the sport.

Watching from the stands in Rotterdam was Biles herself, whose rivalry with Andrade helped define the gymnastics competition at Paris 2024, as Andrade scored 14.466 across two vaults to finish ahead of Americans Claire Pease (14.233) and Skye Blakely (14.166), becoming the first Brazilian gymnast to win three world titles on the same apparatus.

She achieved the victory without attempting the most difficult vaults of her career, performing a Yurchenko double twist and a Lopez, with execution scores of 9.400 and 9.333, respectively.

Speaking to Brazilian outlet ge afterwards, Andrade said the result demonstrated that adjustments to her training were working, expressing pride at winning without needing her highest-difficulty skills.

Two years earlier, Andrade had pushed Biles throughout the Paris Olympics, finishing second to the American in the all-around final. After retaining her title, Biles told French newspaper L'Équipe that she had never felt so stressed during a competition, thanking Andrade for the challenge.

The Brazilian finished 1.199 points behind Biles in the all-around final, with the American's higher-difficulty routines proving decisive as Andrade remained within striking distance.

Biles subsequently joked about being tired of competing against the Brazilian, but Andrade would have her revenge in the floor final, beating Biles by just 0.033 points to become Olympic champion.

The medal ceremony produced one of the enduring images of the Games, with Biles and American team-mate Jordan Chiles bowing towards Andrade as she stood on the top step of the podium.

Andrade left Paris with four medals, including all-around and vault silver and team bronze alongside her floor gold, bringing her Olympic total to six and making her the most decorated Brazilian Olympian in history. Her career, though, had already been interrupted by three anterior cruciate ligament injuries and five knee operations, with the physical demands of competing across four apparatus becoming increasingly difficult to sustain.

After winning floor gold on Aug. 5, 2024, Andrade did not compete again for 22 months, missing the 2025 World Championships in Jakarta before beginning a carefully managed return ahead of Los Angeles 2028.

Her long-time coach, Francisco Porath Neto (known as Chico), acknowledged uncertainty about whether she would rediscover the desire to compete, telling the Brazilian gymnastics federation that both he and Andrade had experienced doubts during her absence, according to NBC Sports .

Andrade returned in June at the Pan American Championships in Rio de Janeiro, competing only on vault and topping qualification with an average of 14.549 before winning the final with 14.266, while helping Brazil secure team silver.

Her comeback, however, came with a significant sacrifice, having announced in August 2025 that she would stop competing on floor because of the strain its tumbling passes and repeated landings placed on her knees.

Speaking to Brazilian outlet UOL after Saturday's final, Andrade reaffirmed that decision, explaining that the apparatus remained physically demanding and that she and Porath had agreed to respect her body's limitations.

The decision effectively ends her participation in the all-around, where she won Olympic silver in Tokyo as well, unless she reverses course before Los Angeles.

Instead, her focus has shifted towards specialist events and helping Brazil remain competitive in team gymnastics, with ge reporting that uneven bars are scheduled to return to her programme in 2027.

In Rotterdam, Andrade competed on vault and balance beam but did not attempt to qualify for the all-around final, while contributing scores of 14.400 and 13.433, respectively, in Wednesday's team final.

Brazil finished fifth behind China, the United States, Japan and France, a step back from the team's historic Olympic bronze in Paris and world silver in Antwerp in 2023.

Andrade's individual victory nevertheless added another world gold to a collection that began with vault gold in Kitakyushu, Japan, in 2021 and an all-around title in Liverpool the following year, before she reclaimed the vault crown in Antwerp in 2023.

Her journey began in Guarulhos, outside São Paulo, where she grew up alongside seven siblings, raised by her mother, Rosa Santos, who worked as a domestic cleaner.

Accounts of her childhood have described the financial difficulties her family faced in getting her to training, with her brother Emerson helping her make the journey before she moved away from home at a young age to pursue gymnastics.

Andrade eventually became Brazil's first female Olympic artistic gymnastics champion with vault gold at Tokyo 2020 and also won all-around silver behind American Suni Lee, before emerging as the closest rival to Biles at the Paris Games.

Biles, 29, has not competed since Paris and has yet to confirm whether she will return for Los Angeles , leaving open the possibility that the two may never compete against each other again.

Andrade expressed appreciation for the American's presence in Rotterdam, telling UOL that Biles could have spent her time elsewhere but had chosen to support the gymnasts competing at the championships.

For Andrade, the next Olympics will involve a different challenge from Paris, when she pushed Biles across four apparatus before eventually beating her on floor. Her latest world title suggests she may not need to reproduce all of that gymnastics to remain among the best in the world.

articles.title: Kwizera y Laura Luego pulverizan los récords de España del medio maratón en Valencia
articles.standfirst: El español para el crono el 58:03 y destroza la marca de Carlos Mayo (59:39) logrado también en Valencia en 2023 y la extremeña (1:08.28) supera la marca de Carla Gallardo
articles.summary: El español para el crono el 58:03 y destroza la marca de Carlos Mayo (59:39) logrado también en Valencia en 2023 y la extremeña (1:08.28) supera la marca de Carla Gallardo
articles.body: Un español ganando el medio maratón de Valencia. Ya ha llovido. Y logrando un tiempo espectacular. Récord de España y fiesta en las calles de la ciudad del Turia. La marca de Kwizera (58:03) pulverizó el registro de Carlos Mayo logrado hace cuatro años también en Valencia en más de un minuto y medio. Un espectáculo. En una carrera en la que salió con todo desde el principio y junto al también español Thierry Ndikumenayo que acabó segundo quedándose a tres segundos del récord de Europa de Andreas Almgren. Kwizera se lleva el récord de España, pero no el de Europa por tema de papeleo. Curiosamente, pese a contar ya con la nacionalidad española desde el pasado verano no ha recibido todavía el 'transfer' internacional de World Athletics, por lo que, aunque puede competir como español en las pruebas nacionales, todavía no está reconocido a efectos internacionales. "Estoy feliz con la marca. Ndikimuneyo y yo hemos preparado juntos en Etiopía la carrera y nos ha salido bien. Queríamos el récord de España y bajar de 58.00. Quería correr más rápido, pero he tenido que tirar todos los kilómetros y al final estaba un poco cansado. La próxima vez batiré el récord de Europa, ahora mismo no podía ser". Pero el medio maratón Valencia escondía otra sorpresa. Laura Luego, que llegó desde atrás en plena remontada ante una Mertixell Soler que habñia salido como un tiro, también batió el récord de España en una recta final agónica que le dio la mejor marca nacional por sólo dois segundos de margen. La extremaña fue un avión y bajó la marca de Carla Gallardo (1:08:30) logrado en Berlin el pasado mes de marzo. La prueba general la ganó Sheila Chepkirui en un emocionante sprint final que le llevó a marcar el mejor crono mundial de la temporada. "Pensaba que podía correr cerca del récord de España, pero tenía dudas porque estoy preparando el maratón. He sacado petróleo de una situación que no era ideal. Quería venir sin liebre para ver el nivel que tenía y guisármelo yo. Me he quedado solo hasta la parte final. En el kilómetro 16 he visto a Meritxell y he seguido empujando. He apretado al final y ha sido un poco agónico pero se ha logrado" Como suele ser habitual, el medio maratón de Valencia Trinidad Alfonso volvió a ser una prueba para 'velocistas'. Hasta doce corredores masculinos bajaron de la hora, una auténtica barbaridad y hasta seis mujeres corrieron por debajo de la hora y cinco minutos, las dos primeras rebajando la mejor marca mundial del año.

articles.title: Swapping horses for ninja warriors: The Olympic sport undergoing massive change
articles.summary: Several Olympic sports have evolved over the years to keep up with an ever-changing landscape, but few have been as drastic as the Modern Pentathlon.
articles.body: Several Olympic sports have evolved over the years to keep up with an ever-changing landscape, but few have been as drastic as the Modern Pentathlon. Ahead of the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028, the ancient sport has modernized yet again – in a way you might not expect. Until recently, the event consisted of the following five disciplines: fencing, horse riding, swimming, shooting and running. But in recent years, the International Modern Pentathlon Union (UIPM) has looked to overhaul the sport’s image, injecting youth and greater accessibility into a sport which has roots in Ancient Greece. The headline from all the changes is the decision to drop horse riding and replace it with obstacle racing – Ninja Warrior style. “While yes, we are a sport with more than a century of Olympic heritage, our recent innovations have made us more vibrant, more accessible and more relevant – ready to connect with new generations,” UIPM President Rob Stull said in a press release. “I like to say that we are one of the ‘cool kids in LA.’” Obstacle racing will still be accompanied by swimming and fencing, with the final discipline being a combination of running and laser shooting (a slight modernization in itself). And while not everyone has been happy with such a major shift, notably all those pentathletes who spent years honing their equestrian skills, the sport deemed it a necessary disturbance in order to maintain its status as an Olympic event. As a result of the change, obstacle racing now operates under the UIPM umbrella and holds its own specific championships. That’s attracted a host of new athletes to Modern Pentathlon – or, in the case of the Beckstrands, an entire family. Real life Ninja Warriors Based out of Utah, brothers Kai and Luke Beckstrand are two of the best obstacle runners in the world. They sprang to prominence on the television show American Ninja Warrior and have since become the face of the Modern Pentathlon’s attempted glow-up. Both have been immersed in the sport since they first learned to walk and were introduced to obstacles by their parents. The family now runs an obstacle gym that allows the brothers to train whenever they want. They now spend up to six hours a day honing their craft. “We already have that skill when it comes to getting on the obstacles. It’s now become about training those transition points and how we can be as efficient as possible getting from obstacle to obstacle, not necessarily the obstacle itself,” Kai, 20, tells CNN Sports over video call while explaining how training with his younger brother allows them both to push each other to new levels. “We do a lot of weightlifting, plyometric-style explosive movements and rock climbing to, kind of, just keep our grip strength good.” Attributes, it’s fair to say, that are quite different from those needed to excel in equestrian. That’s very much the issue facing existing modern pentathletes who have had to quickly learn how to excel across the obstacles. It’s perhaps unsurprising that such a big change did not go down well with everyone. “People say you are making modern pentathlon modern again, but you can’t make that argument when sports like archery are still in the Olympics,” British athlete Joe Choong said back in 2024. “We will still have a sport called modern pentathlon, but it is not the real one.” But while the sport’s new look will take some getting used to, organizers believe the changes will be worth the obvious issues they create if it repositions itself as a younger and sharper Olympic event. And for the brothers, the collaboration is also a chance to promote obstacle racing and their passion for the discipline – essentially piggybacking on Modern Pentathlon’s long history and established audience. “The hope for us is to get it as its own discipline, so that we can compete in the Olympics as well,” Kai says. “But if we can get more eyes from the American Ninja Warrior TV show, that may not even know what the Modern Pentathlon is, that’s going to get more eyes on it. I think it’s a little more exciting than the horse jumping. “With the obstacles, you’re not reliant on your horse. You’re reliant on your own abilities. Coming into this competition, it’s solely based on your performance now.” A multi-discipline barrier However, the brothers – and other obstacle athletes – share a similar problem with those legacy modern pentathletes. Heading into LA 2028, neither believes they have the skills to compete in the other four disciplines, making the Olympics a distant dream… for now. “I think I’ve definitely thought of [training for the Olympics], but when we went to go try swimming, try those other disciplines, we weren’t the greatest,” Luke Beckstrand, 18, says while sitting next to his brother “I know we’ll get better as we train, but I just think we are really busy with our schedules and more focused on the obstacle portion of the pentathlon.” His older brother, Kai, has similar thoughts while also balancing his current training with work as a firefighter. “We’re just, kind of, in a position right now where we don’t have anywhere to train those other disciplines,” the 20-year-old said. So while the sport is trying something different in order to survive in an ever-changing Olympic landscape, it’s by no means going to be a guaranteed success overnight. The talent gap that now exists across the sport needs time to close while athletes come to terms with a very different discipline. It should, though, make for interesting viewing when the LA Olympics roll around in 2028.

articles.title: Kawano y Henderson baten los récords mundiales de maratón marcha
articles.standfirst: El japonés, con 3.14:52, y la australiana, con 2.55:14, superan las plusmarcas universales de la distancia en la All Japan Race Walking que se disputó este domingo en Takahata
articles.summary: El japonés, con 3.14:52, y la australiana, con 2.55:14, superan las plusmarcas universales de la distancia en la All Japan Race Walking que se disputó este domingo en Takahata
articles.body: El japonés Masatora Kawano y la australiana Rebecca Henderson batieron este domingo sendos récords mundiales de maratón marcha, con 2.55:14 y 3.14:52, respectivamente, logrados en la reunión All Japan Race Walking, un evento de bronce del World Athletics Race Walking Tour, en Takahata. Kawano logró el primer récord mundial masculino de la distancia, ya que se convirtió en prueba oficial en enero de 2026. Entonces se estableció una marca de 2.56:30 para el registro universal inaugural en la prueba, que ha superado este domingo el marchador japonés. Por su parte, Henderson mejoró el récord mundial femenino de 3.15:11, que estableció Sofia Fiorini en el Campeonato Europeo de Birmingham que se disputó el pasado agosto.

articles.title: El marchador Marc Tur anuncia su retirada a los 31 años
articles.standfirst: Cuarto en los 50 km marcha de los Juegos de Tokio, se ha posicionado como portavoz del colectivo LGTBI
articles.summary: Cuarto en los 50 km marcha de los Juegos de Tokio, se ha posicionado como portavoz del colectivo LGTBI
articles.body: El balear Marc Tur, campeón del mundo de 20 kilómetros marcha por equipos en 2024 en Turquía, anunció su retirada del atletismo profesional a los 31 años, una "decisión difícil de asumir". Marc Tur, licenciado en Medicina y firme defensor públicamente de los derechos del colectivo LGTBIQ+, fue elegido en 2022 mejor atleta español masculino por la Real Federación Española de Atletismo (RFEA). "Decir adiós, un adiós definitivo cuesta mucho. Es difícil asumirlo. Sabía que había llegado el momento de colgar las zapatillas. Ha llegado la hora de la retirada deportiva. No hay más orgullo que poder representar a tu pueblo y a tu isla. No puedo estar más feliz de cerrar este ciclo donde empezó todo y junto a la gente que más quiero", dijo el atleta en un acto organizado por la SCR Peña Deportiva y el ayuntamiento ibicenco de Santa Eulalia. Marc Tur se despide del atletismo con un diploma olímpico en los 50 kilómetros marcha de los Juegos de Tokio 2021, en los que fue cuarto y se quedó a un paso del bronce. Además formó parte del equipo español que logró el título mundial en los 20 kilómetros marcha de Antalya (Turquía) en 2024, también se proclamó campeón de Europa por equipos con el combinado nacional en 2021 y logró ser campeón nacional de los 50 kilómetros marcha en 2019.

articles.title: Los 'vikingos' se llevan la 'Décima' en el Derbi de las aficiones
articles.standfirst: Rodrigo Mendoza, con nuevo récord (28:16), y Carla Martínez (33:16) se hacen con el triunfo en el Derbi de las Aficiones AliExpress Marcas+ Chuwi, con más de 10.000 corredores
articles.summary: Rodrigo Mendoza, con nuevo récord (28:16), y Carla Martínez (33:16) se hacen con el triunfo en el Derbi de las Aficiones AliExpress Marcas+ Chuwi, con más de 10.000 corredores
articles.body: Los 'Vikingos' mandan de nuevo en la capital. Más de 10.000 corredores han tomado las calles de Madrid en el Derbi de las Aficiones AliExpress Marcas+ Chuwi, uno de los 10k homologados más rápidos de la ciudad. Fue de nuevo el derbi del buen rollo, del pique sano y de la deportividad, en el que 'indios' y 'vikingos' defienden sus colores en el asfalto. Con salida junto al Bernabéu y meta en el paseo de los Melancólicos, junto al antiguo Vicente Calderón, el recorrido favorable, de perfil descendente y con paso por lugares emblemáticos como Cibeles, Neptuno, Atocha o Pirámides, hace el resto para motivar a todos los corredores a dar el máximo, conseguir una gran marca individual e impulsar a su equipo hacia la victoria. En este escenario, Rodrigo Mendoza se convirtió en el absoluto rey de esta edición del Derbi de las Aficiones AliExpress Marcas+ Chuwi. Dominador de principio a fin y corriendo en solitario, destrozó el récord de la prueba que ostentaba Alejandro Jiménez con un espectacular tiempo en meta: 28:16. El podio lo completó el doble ganador del Derbi, Nicolás Regidor (29:05) y Sergio Salinero (29:16). En la prueba femenina, Carla Martínez se impuso representando a los 'Vikingos'. Su tiempo en meta fue 33:16, seguida de Laura Martínez Cabañas (33:39) y Nadine López (34:39). Un podio plenamente blanco, que hacía augurar un buen resultado global para los Vikingos. La magia del Derbi de las Aficiones AliExpress Marcas+ Chuwi es que no sólo hay dos ganadores. Todos los participantes, con independencia de sus marcas, pueden conseguir la victoria y ser las estrellas de este partido. Y es que todos los corredores y las corredoras, al inscribirse, eligen un bando: 'Indios' o 'Vikingos'. Se corre de forma individual, pero el tiempo de cada participante cuenta. Y el equipo que consigue el menor tiempo medio se hace con el título. En esta edición, los campeones fueron los 'Vikingos', que con un tiempo medio de 51:12, superaron en poco menos de un minuto a unos combativos Indios para firmar su 'Décima. Con esta victoria, el marcador del Derbi de las Aficiones® AliExpress Marcas+ Chuwi se pone 10-6, para dejar claro que si hablamos de correr, el jugador número 12 de los Vikingos está imparable. Esta fiesta, con un marcado tinte futbolero, tuvo a AliExpress Marcas+ Chuwi como patrocinador principal, y contó con el impulso de Cabify, BM Supermercados y el concesionario Toyota Hersamotor, además de la colaboración del Ayuntamiento de Madrid. articles.title: Lucas Pinheiro manda un potente mensaje a Marco Odermatt
articles.standfirst: El brasileño, mejor gigantista de la pasada temporada y oro olímpico, se impone con autoridad en el Gigante de Sölden, la prueba que abre la Copa del Mundo
articles.summary: El brasileño, mejor gigantista de la pasada temporada y oro olímpico, se impone con autoridad en el Gigante de Sölden, la prueba que abre la Copa del Mundo
articles.body: El viento azotó el glaciar Rettenbach y el arranque de la Copa del Mundo para los hombres estuvo en vilo. Hubo que bajar bastante la salida y recortar mucho el trazado respecto al de ayer para las mujeres. Pero finalmente se dio luz verde Con la nieve blanda en muchos tramos, fueron los primeros dorsales los que aprovecharon las mejores condiciones de la pista. Porque el trazado iba a empezar a pasar factura pronto. El que mejor leyó la primera manga, marcada por el equipo noruego, fue Lucas Pinheiro, ganador del Globo de Gigante la pasada temporada. El brasileño fue de menos a más. El ritmo de su último sector destrozó a sus rivales. Por quinta vez en Gigante iba a firmar el mejor tiempo al acabar la primera manga. En cuatro de las anteriores terminó ganando la prueba. Y la segunda manga la marcaba su equipo. Al tiempo del brasileño de Oslo (52.40) se acercaron Loïc Meillard (+0.24) y Stefan Brennsteiner (+0.49), pero, a excepción del suizo, las distancias se hicieron profundas. El gran rey, Marco Odermatt, tuvo en el sector intermedio un comportamiento en exceso preventivo. Peor que el brasileño en cada tramo, se fue por encima del medio segundo. Pero es Odermatt y quedaba el interrogante del daño que podía hacer el deterioro de la pista durante la segunda manga. Sin españoles en el corte final (Aleix Aubert se quedó muy cerca, en el puesto 32, y Aingeru Garay se fue al 53), la segunda manga se puso en marcha bajo bandera alemana, la de Anton Grammel. Y con los interrogantes del viento, la luz y la reacción de la pista. A la espera de la salida de los gallos que iban a pelear por la primera victoria de la temporada, la afición local se dio una alegría al ver a uno de los suyos, Raphael Haaser, colocarse al mando. No duró demasiado. La siguiente bandera en tomar el liderato fue la de Estados Unidos, gracias a River Radamus. Al corte de los diez mejores, que marcaba el tiempo del francés Thibaut Favrot, se llegó con River Radamus sentado en el sillón reservado para el líder. Con la pista exigiendo cada vez más, el crono del esquiador de Edwards (Colorado) seguía al mando cuando solo faltaban por bajar los cinco mejores. Con el noruego McGrath fuera nada más salir, Radamus ya era, como mínimo, quinto. Oteaba algo que en su carrera solo había logrado una vez: tocar el podio. Eso lo hizo en casa, en Palisades Tahoe, en marzo de 2024. Ganar no iba a poder, porque Marco Odermatt rebajó su tiempo en 33 centésimas. El ogro enseñaba sus fauces a sus rivales. Con la grada entregada, a Brennsteiner se lo comió la presión. De su tercer mejor tiempo pasó a ser noveno. Ya solo quedaban dos: Meillard y Pinheiro. El suizo, elegante en cada movimiento sobre la pista, tuvo una bajada de menos a más. Acabó como un cohete y rebajó en una centésima el tiempo de Odermatt. Pinheiro, el mejor gigantista de la temporada pasada, ofreció una bajada imponente. El mensaje está lanzado: tanto por la victoria como por la manera de lograrla. Odermatt ya sabe que va a tener que sudar. Y mucho. En Sölden, donde hasta ahora su mejor resultado había sido una cuarta plaza, Pinheiro encabezó el podio, con Meillard segundo y Odermatt cerrándolo. "Mi trabajo durante la pretemporada se ha centrado en convencerde de que puedo superar la temporada pasada", explicaba a Eurosport el brasileño. De momento, el primer mensaje es potente.

articles.title: Moscow to host 2030 World Weightlifting Championships
articles.summary: The International Weightlifting Federation becomes the first Olympic federation to choose Russia to host a world championships since its invasion of Ukraine.
articles.body:
Moscow will host the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships - the first time an Olympic federation has chosen to stage a global event in Russia since the country's invasion of Ukraine began in 2022.

The International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) announced its decision on Sunday, four months after confirming Russian athletes would again be eligible to compete in its events.

In July, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) provisionally lifted a suspension on the Russian Olympic Committee.

That suspension had been imposed following the country's invasion of Ukraine.

The IOC's subsequent decision potentially opened the way for Russian athletes to compete for their country at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

The IWF announced the host cities of four world championships at junior, youth and senior levels, awarding the 2029 senior event to Ahmedabad in India.

"All the bids we received were excellent and we are sure that the championships in your respective countries will be a huge success," said IWF general secretary Jose Quinones.

No world championships in an Olympic sport, summer or winter, have been held in Russia since the start of the war in Ukraine.

The 2025 World Aquatics Championships, initially awarded to the Russian city of Kazan, were instead moved to Singapore.

Moscow has not held the World Weightlifting Championships since 1983.

The Russian Weightlifting Federation said: "[We are] the first Olympic sports federation to succeed in bringing a top-level official competition back to the country in many years."

Federation president Aleksandr Vinokurov thanked the IWF in a post on Telegram "for their trust", with the championships also serving as a qualifying event for the 2032 Olympic Games in Brisbane, Australia.

"Russia has all the necessary experience and capabilities to host competitions of the highest level," he said.

"Moscow has repeatedly staged major international sporting events and has modern infrastructure."

In announcing its decision in July to provisionally lift Russia's suspension, the IOC said that no decision had been taken on whether Russia could display their flag, colours and anthem at the Olympic ‌Games.

The IOC said it would continue to "not organise IOC events in Russia or invite Russian government or state officials to its events".

Some Russian athletes competed at the 2024 Paris Olympic Games and this year's Winter Olympics in Milan as neutrals.

Ukraine filed an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) requesting that the IOC decision to lift its suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee be annulled.

The IOC's move decision came after the International Paralympic Committee had already ended Russia's exile from global sports events, with the country's athletes allowed to compete under their national flag at the Winter Paralympics.

Five Ukrainian athletes are listed to compete in the 2026 IWF World Championships in Ningbo, China, which are scheduled to take place from 27 October to 8 November.

articles.summary: El empresario asegura al término de la media maratón de Valencia que este será el último año en el que el premio esté en vigor y todos miran a Kejelcha
articles.body: será este año... o no será. La carrera por el millón de euros toca a su fin. articles.title: Russia to host 2030 World Weightlifting Championships
articles.summary: Russia has been awarded its first world championship in an Olympic sport since the start of the Ukraine war, with Moscow set to host the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships
articles.body:
The International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) confirmed the news on Sunday, four months after it announced Russian and Belarusian athletes would be eligible to compete in IWF events.

The Federation added that Ahmedabad, India, will host the 2029 World Weightlifting Championships.

"All the bids we received were excellent and we are sure that the Championships in your respective countries will be a huge success," IWF General Secretary Jose Quinones said.

"It is also worth noting that three of these four countries will be organising an IWF world event for the first time - Kosovo, Venezuela and India.

"This demonstrates our sport is growing worldwide and the staging of our competitions is highly desirable for many nations around the planet."

In July, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) provisionally lifted its suspension on Russian athletes, a move that could see some become eligible to compete at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

The move ended a ban that had been in place since 2023 following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The 2025 World Athletics Championships, which were set to be hosted in Kazan, were subsequently moved to Singapore.

During that period, the Russian flag and anthem have not been seen or heard at summer Olympic events, and only some athletes from the country have been able to compete as neutrals.

IOC President Kirsty Coventry said the decision was to "ensure all athletes have the possibility to compete at the games and not be held responsible for their government's actions".

Coventry also added the IOC would not be staging competitions in Russia or invite government officials to its events, but would allow international federations to make their own decisions on hosting of events.

In September 2025, the International Paralympic Committee (IPC) allowed Russian and Belarusian athletes to compete under their country's national flags at the Milano Cortina Winter Paralympic Games in 2026.

The IWF slowly began lifting restrictions on Russian and Belarusian athletes in 2026, first removing suspensions for youth and junior athletes earlier in the year, before announcing in June that athletes across all age categories would be eligible to compete.

The 2026 World Weightlifting Championships get underway on October 27 in Ningbo, China, with seven Ukrainian Athletes currently listed to compete.

articles.title: Asian Champions Trophy: Hockey returns to Punjab after 17 years as India eye another ACT title
articles.summary: India will begin their campaign as favourites when the Asian Champions Trophy (ACT) gets underway in Punjab on Tuesday.
articles.body: India will begin their campaign as favourites when the Asian Champions Trophy (ACT) gets underway in Punjab on Tuesday. The five-time champions will face Bangladesh in their opening match, looking to build on their gold-medal-winning performance at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya.The tournament is special for another reason. International hockey is returning to Punjab after a gap of 17 years, giving several Indian players a chance to play in front of their families and home fans.The last international hockey tournament held in the state was the Gold Cup in 2009.A special occasion for Punjab's hockey starsPunjab has played a major role in Indian hockey for decades. More than half of the current Indian team comes from the state, which has produced several leading players over the years.India captain Harmanpreet Singh, Jugraj Singh, Jarmanpreet Singh, Rajinder Singh, Hardik Singh, Sukhjeet Singh, Dilpreet Singh and Mandeep Singh will get the opportunity to play in their home state in front of family and friends.For Harmanpreet, having his family in the stands is expected to make the occasion even more special.The tournament will also bring back memories of some of India's greatest hockey players, including Balbir Singh Senior, Udham Singh Kular, Prithipal Singh, Ajit Pal Singh, Surjit Singh Randhawa and Pargat Singh.Sansarpur village in Jalandhar is often called the 'Mecca of Indian hockey'. It has produced 14 Olympians and around 300 other national and international players.India chief coach Craig Fulton is also looking forward to the team's return to Punjab."...we can't wait to feed off the home crowd. Young defender Amandeep Lakra and midfielder Aditya Lalage have also been given opportunities to prove themselves at the international level.India will start against Bangladesh, who replaced Pakistan after the latter withdrew from the tournament, citing security reasons.After the opening match, India will face China on October 29, Japan on October 30, Malaysia on November 1 and Korea on November 2.The top four teams in the league stage will qualify for the semifinals. The semifinals and final will be held in Mohali on November 4 and 5.Malaysia and Japan could test IndiaWith Pakistan absent, Malaysia are expected to pose the biggest challenge to India. The two sides have had tough battles in the past, and India cannot afford to take the Malaysians lightly.India beat Malaysia 5-1 in the Asian Games final, but the upcoming tournament will provide another test for Harmanpreet and his teammates.Korea have struggled to maintain their earlier standing in international hockey, but Japan remain capable of upsetting stronger teams. articles.title: Youth Olympic Games: All you need to know about Dakar 2026
articles.summary: Senegal hosts Africa's first Olympic event as the Dakar 2026 Youth Games bring together 2,700 athletes from around the world.
articles.body:
On Saturday, 31 October the Olympic rings will be raised for an event hosted on African soil for the first time as Senegal stages the Youth Olympic Games.

The cities of Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly will host 15 days of competition running until 13 November.

About 2,700 athletes are set to compete across 25 sports, with 153 medal events.

There will also be 10 engagement sports held without medals awarded.

Organised by the International Olympic Committee (IOC), the event is an elite multi-sport competition for athletes predominantly aged from 15 to 17.

The aim is not only to inspire young people, but also to promote Olympic values and encourage them to see sport as a vehicle for peace and solidarity.

First held in Singapore in 2010, the Youth Olympics contain several elements of the senior Games but add newer sports, mixed-gender events and cultural activities.

Nanjing, China, staged the second edition in 2014 and Argentina's capital Buenos Aires was the venue four years later.

Dakar was due to host in 2022 before the Covid-19 pandemic forced its postponement.

Since its inception, several participants have gone on to top the podium at the Olympic Games.

South African swimmer Chad le Clos and British taekwondo athlete Jade Jones featured at the the inaugural edition in Singapore and two years later became Olympic champions at London 2012.

American sprinter Noah Lyles claimed 200m gold in Nanjing 12 years ago before winning 100m gold at the Paris 2024 Olympics.

Having the Youth Olympics in Senegal is "monumental" for the continent, according to IOC official Christophe Dubi.

"Africa has hosted many international competitions but this is the first time we have anything labelled with the Olympic rings," he told BBC Sport Africa.

Thierno Cisse, deputy chief operating officer of the Local Organising Committee (LOC), says the whole country feels the weight of the moment.

"We know we are going to be ambassadors for Africa," he said.

"It's really important for us to proudly represent the whole continent and show that Africa has high standards."

There is another link to the top of the Olympic movement.

Zimbabwe's Kirsty Coventry, who last year became the first woman and first African to be elected president of the IOC, previously chaired the coordination commission for Dakar 2026.

Youth unemployment remains a pressing issue across much of Africa, the world's youngest continent, including in Senegal.

While some residents remain sceptical, organisers hope these Games can provide both immediate and longer-term benefits through employment, tourism, volunteer programmes and skills development.

More than 400 young Africans have already received training in event operations, logistics, technology, accreditation and venue management.

"The impact will be much wider," Dubi claimed. "It starts with sports and this is where it will permeate across the continent."

What sports will feature at the Youth Olympics?

Nineteen of the 25 competition sports, including athletics, swimming and more youth-focused events like breaking and skateboarding, are ones which were held at the Paris 2024 Olympics.

Beach handball, beach wrestling, futsal and rowing coastal beach sprints are also included alongside Baseball5 and Wushu Taolu, which are both making their debut at the Youth Olympics.

Baseball5, an urban, simplified version of traditional baseball requiring no equipment, will kick off competition at Dakar 2026 on Friday, 30 October.

Wushu Taolu is a modern Chinese martial art practiced competitively via choreographed sequences and sparring, while the coastal rowing takes place on the sea, unlike traditional Olympic rowing.

Golf, karate and surfing are among the 10 engagement sports staged to encourage participation among locals.

Climbing, hockey, modern pentathlon, paddlesport (canoe slalom and canoe sprint), shooting, tennis and weightlifting round out the events intended to deliver gender equality across the Youth Olympics for the first time.

Africa prepares for historic Olympic moment at Dakar 2026

Rather than constructing an expensive collection of new venues, organisers have focused on renovating and repurposing existing facilities that can continue serving local communities after the Games.

Dakar hosts athletics, rugby sevens and futsal at the historic Iba Mar Diop complex, while swimming, 3x3 basketball, breaking, skateboarding and Baseball5 will take place at the waterfront Tour de l'Oeuf complex.

Road cycling races will be staged along the Corniche Ouest.

The new city of Diamniadio , being developed south east of Dakar, will serve as the operational heart of the Games.

The Abdoulaye Wade Stadium there will host the opening ceremony and archery competition, with badminton at the Dakar Arena.

The Dakar Expo Centre welcomes gymnastics, fencing, table tennis, judo and Wushu Taolu.

Senegal's Atlantic coastline in Saly provides the backdrop for sailing, triathlon, beach handball and coastal rowing at Saly Plage Ouest.

The Games are also designed as a celebration of Senegalese and African culture.

The mascot Ayo, a young lion, was designed by a student while another chose the name from the Yoruba word meaning joy.

The Dakar 2026 medals feature a lion on one side and a baobab tree on the other, with the images intended to represent both Senegal and Africa's heritage, resilience and longevity.

The official song 'Teranga', the Wolof word for hospitality, is performed by Senegalese artist Mamy Mbaye, and the athletes' village programme includes lessons in traditional sabar and djembe drumming and dance.

The Olympic flame was lit in Athens on 10 September and reached Dakar two days later. Since then it has travelled around 3,600km through all 14 regions of Senegal, with about 450 torchbearers over 30 stages.

The tour ends on 30 October at Place de la Nation in Dakar before the flame lights the cauldron at the opening ceremony a day later.

Nigerian wrestling star Blessing Oborududu and Algerian Olympic gymnastics champion Kaylia Nemour are among those who have been recruited to inspire competitors.

Ambassadors for the Games include Senegal football captain Kalidou Koulibaly, Kenyan marathon legend Eliud Kipchoge and social media star Khaby Lame.

Kipchoge has taken on a particularly significant role, mentoring the refugee team making its debut at a Youth Olympics, having been introduced at the senior Games at Rio 2016.

Six young athletes, identified through trials and development programmes in East Africa , will compete in athletics, judo and taekwondo, and receive education and wellbeing support.

Neither the LOC nor the IOC could provide a figure on what the Games will cost when asked by the BBC, but Senegal's government committed to spend at least $60m (£44.8m) as part of the host contract.

There are also loans, thought to have increased to around $90m (£67.2m), being spent on long-term sports infrastructure projects.

The Abdoulaye Wade Stadium, which opened in 2022 , cost a reported $270m (£202m).

A post-Games impact report should reveal the ultimate cost, but both the LOC and IOC say the event should be judged by its legacy.

"The Games are opening a whole range of new sports that are not famous here," said Cisse.

"Maybe we'll be able to say in 20 years from now that some champions were discovered."

For Dubi, the ambition is wider than Senegal.

"It's not only about sport. People will be amazed by what they will see."

That may ultimately be Dakar 2026's greatest achievement: not simply bringing the Olympic rings to Africa for the first time, but allowing the world to experience the movement through an African lens.

articles.title: Three days to deadline, guidelines issued for IOA's SOM nominations
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) Electoral Officer (returning officer), Sanjay K.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) Electoral Officer (returning officer), Sanjay K. Srivastava, has issued guidelines for the Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) elections, warning that nominations that fail to comply with the prescribed conditions will not be considered valid.In the document dated October 26, retired IAS officer Srivastava clarified the nomination procedure and issued a modified Form 2 for candidates seeking election as SOMs to the IOA General Assembly. The deadline remains October 30.The revised instructions place particular emphasis on the role of proposers and seconders, who must be members of the male or female SOM roster published by the Electoral Officer on October 23.An individual can propose or second one candidate in the male category and one in the female category. However, if the same person endorses more than one candidate in either category, the later nomination will be rejected. The instructions also state that a proposer or seconder cannot withdraw their name once the nomination has been delivered.The rules permit cross-gender endorsements: a male SOM can propose or second a female candidate, and a female SOM can do the same for a male candidate. The restriction is on endorsing multiple candidates within the same category, not on the gender of the candidate being nominated.Eight representatives to enter the IOA General AssemblyThe SOM election will determine eight representatives to the IOA General Assembly, comprising four men and four women. Under the IOA’s Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit Rules, 2026, one male and one female representative will subsequently be elected from among the eight to the IOA Executive Council.The SOM framework is designed to incorporate the experience of former elite athletes, including the current president PT Usha, into the governance of Indian sport. Candidates must satisfy the prescribed eligibility conditions, including Indian citizenship, being of sound mind, being between 25 and 70 years of age on the date of application, and having retired from active sport for at least one year before applying. They must also have represented India in an Olympic sport for which the concerned national sports federation or sports body is an IOA member.The next stages of the process will involve scrutiny of nominations, disposal of objections and publication of the final list of contesting candidates. Polling is scheduled for November 9, and will be conducted virtually, with detailed instructions to be issued separately.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Russia given first championships since Ukraine invasion
articles.summary: The International Weightlifting Federation becomes the first Olympic federation to choose Russia to host a world championships since its invasion of Ukraine.
articles.body:
Moscow will host the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships - the first time an Olympic federation has chosen to stage a global event in Russia since the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in 2022.

The International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) announced its decision on Sunday, four months after confirming Russian athletes would again be eligible to compete in its events.

In July, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) provisionally lifted a suspension on the Russian Olympic Committee.

That suspension had been imposed following the country's invasion of Ukraine.

The IOC's subsequent decision potentially opened the way for Russian athletes to compete for their country at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

The IWF announced the host cities of four world championships at junior, youth and senior levels, awarding the 2029 senior event to Ahmedabad in India.

"All the bids we received were excellent and we are sure that the championships in your respective countries will be a huge success," said IWF general secretary Jose Quinones.

No world championships in an Olympic sport, summer or winter, have been held in Russia since the start of the war in Ukraine.

The 2025 World Aquatics Championships, initially awarded to the Russian city of Kazan, were instead moved to Singapore.

Moscow has not held the World Weightlifting Championships since 1983.

The Russian Weightlifting Federation said: "[We are] the first Olympic sports federation to succeed in bringing a top-level official competition back to the country in many years."

Federation president Aleksandr Vinokurov thanked the IWF in a post on Telegram "for their trust", with the championships also serving as a qualifying event for the 2032 Olympic Games in Brisbane, Australia.

"Russia has all the necessary experience and capabilities to host competitions of the highest level," he said.

"Moscow has repeatedly staged major international sporting events and has modern infrastructure."

Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha‎ said the decision was "unacceptable" and "immoral".

Posting on X , Sybiha added: "We must not allow the Kremlin to use international sport to claim recognition, legitimacy or a return to business as usual without ending its aggression or facing accountability."

Meanwhile the country's minister for youth and sports, Matvii Bidnyi, said Ukrainian athletes will boycott the championships if they are held in Moscow.

In announcing its decision in July to provisionally lift Russia's suspension, the IOC said that no decision had been taken on whether Russia could display their flag, colours and anthem at the Olympic ‌Games.

The IOC said it would continue to "not organise IOC events in Russia or invite Russian government or state officials to its events".

Some Russian athletes competed at the 2024 Paris Olympic Games and this year's Winter Olympics in Milan as neutrals.

Ukraine filed an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) requesting that the IOC decision to lift its suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee be annulled.

The IOC's move decision came after the International Paralympic Committee had already ended Russia's exile from global sports events, with the country's athletes allowed to compete under their national flag at the Winter Paralympics.

Five Ukrainian athletes are listed to compete in the 2026 IWF World Championships in Ningbo, China, which are scheduled to take place from 27 October to 8 November.
